articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Philosophers have recently been trying to develop uniform decision rules for instances in which physicians' judgments diverge from the recommendations of medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems. articles.title: Ethics Suppression in AI Development: A Comparative Case Study of Responsible AI Under Competitive Pressure
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This study explores the governance tensions among Google, OpenAI, Meta, and Microsoft, focusing on how competitive AI development can lead to the ethics suppression. The study aims to examine how ethical oversight loses practical influence even when responsible AI structures are formally in place, especially during rapid technological competition. Despite the rapid growth of responsible AI frameworks and ethical principles in the tech sector, there has been less focus on how these concerns are actually applied when pressure to deploy increases.

articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parents, pediatricians, and journalists have raised concern that child-facing videos are becoming increasingly overstimulating, but this concern rests mostly on ad hoc observation rather than systematic measurement. articles.title: Knowing Which, Not How Much: Language Models Order Party Positions They Cannot Place
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.21878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models are increasingly asked where real actors stand: what a party's platform prioritises, what an institution has committed to. articles.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Patient-facing AI triage tools may support care-seeking and emergency department prioritization, but require evaluation beyond acuity accuracy alone. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.22133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Human mobility often declines sharply following disasters and subsequently exhibits complex recovery dynamics.
